title: Modular Multiplicative Inverse
description: Given a non-negative integer `a` and a prime integer `p`, find the unique integer `x` in `[1, p - 1]` such that `(a * x) % p == 1`. If no such modular inverse exists (which happens when `a` is divisible by `p`), return `-1`.
constraints: p is guaranteed to be a prime number.
hints: First reduce `a = a % p`; if `a == 0`, no inverse exists modulo `p`, so return `-1`.
By Fermat's Little Theorem for prime `p`, `a^(p - 1) == 1 (mod p)`, so `a^(-1) == a^(p - 2) (mod p)`, computable via binary exponentiation in O(log p).

examples.explanation: 3 * 5 = 15 == 1 (mod 7), so the inverse of 3 mod 7 is 5.
10 is divisible by 5, so no inverse exists and we return -1.
